dataset_title: Green-leaf fractionation nitrogen yields and fraction nitrogen concentrations
citation: Nynäs, A.-L., Newson, W. R., & Johansson, E. (2021). Protein Fractionation of Green Leaves as an Underutilized Food Source—Protein Yield and the Effect of Process Parameters. Foods, 10(11), 2533.
geography: Southern Sweden field residues and Alnarp campus lucerne; retail spinach sourced from Italy.
field_sample_years: 2017-2018; retail spinach collection date not stated
dataset_scope: 189 tidy source observations: Table 2a initial-biomass-relative N yields (54 rows), Table 2b incoming-fraction-relative step N yields (36 rows), and Table 2c fraction N concentration on a dry-matter basis (99 rows; the unreported carrot P4 value is retained as a blank status row).
materials: Broccoli, cabbage, kale, mangold, beetroot, sugarbeet, carrot leafy residues

process_conditions.feed_preparation: Frozen plant material was thawed and divided into three 300 g process portions.
process_conditions.pressing: Twin-screw pressing; pulp was re-pressed after addition of MilliQ water at 50% of pulp mass (100% for carrot).
process_conditions.particle_separation: Centrifugal separation; reported methods include 11800 RCF for 10 min at 4 C after pressing.
process_conditions.thermal_fractionation: Particle-free juice aliquots (40 mL) had freeze-thaw precipitate removed, were heated at 55 C for 25 min, cooled on ice, then centrifuged.
process_conditions.acid_fractionation: S2 was adjusted to pH 4.5 by dropwise addition of 1 M HCl; acid volume/consumption was not reported.
process_conditions.product_recovery: P3 was resolubilized with water and adjusted to pH 7 using 0.1 M NaOH; residual insoluble fraction P4 was separated.
process_conditions.nitrogen_analysis: Dumas nitrogen analysis of dried samples; the paper reports nitrogen rather than protein because a material-specific N-to-protein factor was unknown.

variable_definitions.table_2a: Nitrogen recovered in each indicated stream as a percentage of nitrogen in the initial biomass.
variable_definitions.table_2b: Nitrogen transfer into each indicated output as a percentage of nitrogen entering that process step; this is a local step denominator and is not interchangeable with Table 2a.
variable_definitions.table_2c: Nitrogen concentration as percent of stream dry matter, not crude-protein content.

uncertainty: Table 2 reports mean ± standard deviation. The table caption states three process replicates unless a superscript gives another replicate count. Blank SDs are left blank where the source gives no SD. Table 2c BM values are transcribed from that panel; no values are copied from Table 1 to replace them.
conversion_method: None. Values, denominators, sample names, and units remain as reported. No conversion from nitrogen to protein and no inferred reagent dosage.
limitations: The study is green leafy biomass fractionation, not roadside grass; lucerne is a forage comparator, not a validated grass proxy.
N yields and N concentrations do not equal protein recovery, product purity, or a full mass balance.
Table 2a and Table 2b have different denominators and must not be combined as if they were the same recovery metric.
A reported step yield above 100% can result from measured fraction variability and is not clipped or normalized.
The pH endpoint and HCl concentration are known, but HCl volume/equivalents per feed or juice are not reported.
Table 2c carrot P4 is unreported; it is blank with reporting_status=not_reported, not zero.
This evidence does not characterize the GreenHub roadside-grass feed, current runtime route, product market grade, or operational scale.
suggested_use: Phase 4 reference evidence for distinguishing nitrogen partition by process stage and fraction nitrogen concentration. Do not use as a GreenHub runtime recovery factor or acid/base demand.
